text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000018's 99215 share remains well above expectation after risk adjustment, yet its few documented 99215 claims mostly support the billed level, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Most of this provider's 99215 volume sits on patients with five or more chronic conditions, and the documented 99215 claims (e.g., C0012364, C0012400, C0012445, C0012463) show high MDM with an unsupported rate matching peers, which is consistent with a genuinely complex panel. However, the risk-adjusted score already accounts for complexity, and the by-complexity table shows the 99215 share running roughly two to five times the all-provider share in every stratum, including patients with no chronic conditions. The billing mix is also almost entirely 99214/99215, with nearly no lower codes. Records cover only 14 claims (about 3% of volume), so the documentation is too thin to clear or confirm the pattern; the absence of no-lab claims among high-data notes gives no cloning signal, but that rests on the same small sample. A reviewer should first obtain a larger, random sample of 99215 records weighted toward the 5+ condition stratum where the excess concentrates, and should also pull the low-complexity 99215s such as C0012483 and C0012524 (same patient, no chronic conditions) and C0012538 (Z09 follow-up only) to test whether visit intensity matches the billed level."}
